title: Stablecoins and Unbacked Crypto-Assets
summary: The design, uses and risks of stablecoins compared with unbacked crypto-assets, with a focus on reserves, redemption and the conditions under which a peg can fail.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: The design, uses and risks of stablecoins compared with unbacked crypto-assets, with a focus on reserves, redemption and the conditions under which a peg can fail.
Learning Objectives: Classify stablecoin types and distinguish them from unbacked crypto-assets
Evaluate reserve, liquidity and redemption risks
Assess governance, disclosure and oversight requirements
Syllabus: Use cases in payments, trading and settlement
Reserve composition, redemption mechanics and stress scenarios
De-pegging, governance failures and transparency red flags
Intended Audience: Supervisors and authorisation staff responsible for, or moving into, oversight of virtual asset service providers
Risk, policy, legal and financial crime specialists working on digital finance
Senior managers shaping the authority's approach to crypto-assets and digital finance
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of financial supervision, authorisation or financial crime work is helpful. No technical background in blockchain or crypto-assets is required.
Core Reading: FSB, High-level Recommendations for the Regulation, Supervision and Oversight of Crypto-Asset Activities and Markets (2023)
IOSCO, Policy Recommendations for Crypto and Digital Asset Markets (2023)
FATF, Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers (2021)
Basel Committee, Prudential Treatment of Cryptoasset Exposures (2022)
